column1: # The ensure plan every catalogue member renders.
# AUTHORED, NOT DUMPED. Every row is derived from three doctrine statements and from
#   substrate_doctrine.md section 3.1 fixes the package-manager root per substrate --
#   Homebrew on apple, the system package manager on linux, winget on windows -- and
#   makes it the one member that is *verified, never installed*, because it cannot be
#   substrate_doctrine.md section 6 fixes the order: ensure the root, ensure ghcup
#   through it, resolve and install the compatible Cabal through ghcup, then the
#   substrate_doctrine.md section 4 fixes who supplies the container engine. Only the
#   native Linux frame installs one; Colima publishes a Docker endpoint as part of
#   creating the Apple guest, and the WSL2 distribution receives the engine the Linux
#   plan installs inside it. So `docker` appears on the two linux rows and on neither
#   of the others -- exactly once per substrate that installs it.
# A version is `$(tool)`, never a number: the pin lives in the authored requirements
# and is substituted at execution, so this file is stable across a bump and can be
# compared at all. A plan that spelled the number here would have two homes.
